greetings.title: Boris Karabut
greetings.description: who ships reliable products with neural nets in the loop, DevOps, testing, and security — without trading away UX or visual craft.

about.title: I build products people trust and enjoy
about.paragraphs: ["I work as a software engineer: I use neural networks in the delivery loop, DevOps to keep releases predictable, and automated tests so quality does not depend on luck. Security is part of the architecture, not a patch at the end.","From the first lines of code in late 2021 I have been growing from interfaces into the full product: architecture, delivery, and the way people actually use what I ship. The north star is still the same — the product has to feel clear, fast, and visually considered.","Every brief is different, so I do not sell a single stack. I pick tools that protect UX and design quality, then wrap them with testing, observability, and secure defaults so the result holds up after launch."]

impact.title: What the work added up to

results: Launched the Startup Cycle project, which got into the Skolkovo startup pre-accelerator.
Developed the service from scratch: I designed the architecture, I chose the technology stack.
Optimized application performance: reduced loading time, improved interface responsiveness.
Covered the code with unit tests (Jest, React Testing Library), increasing the stability of the product.
Participated in the design of new functionality: offered ideas, discussed UX / UI with the team.
Launched a website of the most popular cybersecurity competition in the Russian Federation (CTF Cup)
Launched a website for the sale of merch for participants of CTF competitions and events.
Migrated one of the projects from Vue to React.
Close interacted with all team members (from the designer to the information security specialist).

tools.title: How I ship
tools.lead: Not a catalogue of every library I have opened. Five practices I actually use to keep products fast, safe, and pleasant to use.

interface.title: Interface & design
interface.text: The product has to feel obvious in the hand. I treat layout, motion, and visual hierarchy as part of engineering, not a coat of paint at the end.

ai.title: Neural nets in the loop
ai.text: I use models to speed up research, scaffolding, and review — then I verify the output. AI is a multiplier, not a substitute for judgment.

quality.title: Quality through tests
quality.text: Automated checks around the paths that matter, so regressions show up before users do. Quality is a pipeline, not a final round of clicking.

devops.title: DevOps & delivery
devops.text: Repeatable builds, previews, and releases. If it cannot be shipped the same way twice, it is not done.

security.title: Cybersecurity
security.text: Auth, headers, and threat-aware defaults from the first commit. I come from a CTF community — security is not an afterthought.

projects.title: Projects
projects.descriptions: ["A project with 167+ free developer tools: formatters, converters, validators, cheatsheets for Git, HTTP, Regex, and guides on databases and backend. No registration or payment, all in the browser.","A platform for startup investments: users review project achievements via dashboards and graphs, invest funds, or create their own startup, publishing its progress to attract investments.","A site with complete information for Helldivers 2 players: equipment and weapon stats, the Stratagem Hero mini-game, and a galactic war global map with live event progress.","The site contained event rules, format specifics, required documents, a registration form, and a live stream from the competition.","A platform where CTF community members can buy merchandise with points earned through successful competition results or community activities.","The website of the student IT community at KIPFIN College and Financial University: structure, achievements, rules, and documentation including the official decree establishing the community."]
